html:
The Nepalese royal massacre took place on 1 June 2001 at Narayanhiti Palace in Kathmandu, Nepal, when Crown Prince Dipendra shot dead King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and seven other members of the royal family, then shot himself.

An official inquiry blamed Dipendra, who was said to be drunk and angry over his choice of bride. Many Nepalis never believed it. The throne passed to Birendra's brother Gyanendra, who was unpopular and suspected without proof.

Gyanendra dismissed the government in 2002 and seized full power in 2005 to fight the Maoists of the civil war. The parties and the Maoists united against him, and the revolution of 2006 stripped him of power. Two years later Nepal abolished the monarchy founded by Prithvi Narayan Shah, and the palace became a museum.
sum: The Nepalese royal massacre took place on 1 June 2001 at Narayanhiti Palace in Kathmandu, Nepal, when Crown Prince Dipendra shot dead King Birendra, Queen Aishwarya and seven other members of the royal family, then shot himself.
